Use sliding window for lossless internal pixel buffers

Replace full-height dec->pixels allocations with a sliding row
window bounded by the maximum VP8L backward-reference distance
and copy length. The window is sized to the minimum live rows
(history, the ARGB queue, MAX_LENGTH headroom and the shift
margin); doubling that count only amortized the memmove.

Change-Id: I399190a7c195abc2c506ea53febca5db770a317f

use sliding window for decoded alpha rows

Allocate only a sliding output row window for dec->alpha_plane in
AllocateMemory (frame_dec.c) when alpha dithering is not active.
Drop the ARGB queue and LZ77 copy headroom that the shared VP8L
row helper reserves; the alpha plane is shifted from the rows it
still needs and does not use that pad.

Change-Id: I2a32c3ed493f6e097e573cf5cf0de8a9c96fcfae

coupling: The overflow exists only when both edits are present. ed495e0 sizes VP8LGetWindowRows to min_rows instead of 2*min_rows. min_rows is the documented live-row minimum (history + NUM_ARGB_CACHE_ROWS + ceil-span of MAX_LENGTH + the GetWindowLimit margin), so the lossless pixel buffer is still large enough; the removed factor only amortized ShiftWindow's memmove. On its own the alpha plane still consumes that helper untrimmed, and for the 25-row alpha history the result stays well above the 24 rows plus one retained row that complex filtering writes on the last macroblock row. 8288fde then drops, from the alpha window only, the ARGB queue and LZ77 copy headroom the shared helper adds, because decoded alpha is shifted from min_needed_row and never uses that pad. The pad is recomputed as NUM_ARGB_CACHE_ROWS + ((MAX_LENGTH + width) / width + 1) + 2. That length term matches VP8LGetWindowRows's (MAX_LENGTH + width - 1) / width + 1 for every width that does not divide MAX_LENGTH (4095) and is one row larger when it does. With the helper still doubled, the extra row is absorbed and the trimmed window stays above 25 rows. Together, for a width that divides 4095 (the probe uses 45) and a height above the uncapped min_rows (160 > 135), the helper returns exactly min_rows = 25+16+92+2 = 135 and the trim subtracts 16+93+2 = 111, leaving 24 rows. Uncompressed alpha with the strong filter then writes 24 rows while retaining row-1, one row (width bytes) past the allocation in NoneUnfilter. Restoring either the 2x factor or the canonical ceiling makes the two sites agree and the write lands in-bounds; neither diff is a faulty window by itself, so a fix has to reconcile the helper's row count with the alpha trim.
